summary: Makoto Funaoka is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1965–1969, ~1972–1977) and held positions at the Open University of Japan, Komazawa University, and Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).
Makoto Kitada works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Halle and held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and led Chuo Shoka Junior College (1951).
Makoto Yoshimura is a specialist in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1993–1999) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (~2005).

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held faculty posts at Harvard (1980–1991) and Boston University (1990–2024), among other institutions.
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar. She completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami (1937–2024) was a sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He held several faculty posts at Kyoto University between 1965 and 2001, as well as positions at Kobe and Otani universities.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist. He held positions as DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and Secretary at The Asiatic Society.

Manfred B. Steger works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Robert Baker Aitken and at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers, later holding professorships at Illinois State, RMIT, and the University of Hawaiʻi (2011–2016).

Manfred Mayrhofer (1926–2011) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz (Ph.D.) and served as professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube (1928–2021) specialized in Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Weller at Leipzig University (1949–1953), where he was appointed professor of Tibetan and Mongolian philology in 1991.

Manshi Kiyozawa (1863–1903) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Ernest Fenollosa at the University of Tokyo. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University (~1901–1902).
Manu Leumann (1889–1977) was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein (1862–1943) worked in archaeology, Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and held posts at the Oriental College, University of the Punjab, and Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Lausanne, studying under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and teacher Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Matthew T. Kapstein as doctoral supervisor, as well as Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen (1884–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954), the University of Paris, and L'Humanité.

Marcel Granet (1884–1940) was a sinologist who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held professorships at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1920–1940) and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (~1927–1940), which he founded.

Marcel Mauss (1872–1950) was a scholar of religion and philosophy who studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He served as Directeur d’études at EPHE (1914–1940) and held the Chair of Sociology at Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, and Paul Pelliot. She taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1938–1963) and edited the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
